verdicts.why: No finding is about a length/size field read from untrusted input driving an allocation before the payload is verified to exist. The closest is F02 (integer overflow in timestamp deserialization), which reads a long from the network stream but only multiplies it by 1000 to build a Date; no buffer is sized or allocated from it. F01 is about recursion depth, not allocation.

verdicts.quote: This forms an unbounded mutual recursion with no depth counter or limit.
verdicts.why: F01 describes exactly the cycle mechanism: readFieldValue() calls readTable()/readArray(), which call readFieldValue() again, with no depth counter, so the nesting depth of the attacker-supplied AMQP table/array controls recursion depth.
